historicalLineageReview.method: Read-only ListGrokBotTranscriptEntries and ListGrokBotAgentSessions; response bodies inspected in memory and only whitelisted metadata retained locally.
observations: Automation records contain run IDs and request IDs. Exact run-ID to billed sand-subagent conversation-ID joins remain the proven automation attribution method.
Historical approval records can contain explicit child and parent-agent IDs. A parent-bot link alone does not establish which automation caused a child.
Some raw history contains spend-initiation records that the installed app filters out. Observed rows were message initiated; their names do not imply a billable amount.
Exact automation-run request-ID matches in inspected history confirmed already-known ownership; they did not recover additional automation links.
The session-list response was empty for the sampled account bots. Probing two known billed child IDs as transcript agent IDs returned no entries.
No client-backed automation-run session namespace, complete routine-run pagination, or historical child-to-routine reader was found.
limits: Incomplete sampled historical reads do not prove that every backend record or endpoint lacks richer metadata.
The longest observed routine run lists contained 20 entries. A rolling cap is suggested, not a verified server implementation.
Retaining exact observed links improves future history but cannot reconstruct links never observed.
No installed app, routine, model, billing setting, telemetry setting, or server data was modified.

routineIdentityNamespaces.finding: These fields intentionally have distinct namespaces. The native list exposes the parsed record ID, while webhook credential lookup finds the enclosing row by that ID and sends its server automationId. Differences are not conflicting ownership. A missing local record ID stays unknown.
routineIdentityNamespaces.evidence: Independent inspection of the installed list parser and webhook credential request builder; separate live metadata read confirmed different IDs on ordinary records.

localAutomationCacheReview.result: No structured historical automation ownership recovered from account-scoped local storage.
sourceObservations: The renderer automation store is an in-memory Map. Refresh replaces its installed record arrays and reset clears them.
Registered persistent slices do not include an automation/routine slice.
diskObservations: Account-scoped persistence blobs contained no structured record.id to runs[].id ownership candidates.
The inspected Local Storage and Session Storage had no candidate routine record fields or SST history; no IndexedDB directory was present.
localAutomationCacheReview.limit: This is a bounded observation of the selected installation, not proof that every provider version or backend lacks historical records.
localAutomationCacheReview.action: Read-only static and local metadata inspection; no application mutation or new authenticated request.
